prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "colorize", with the standing line "Walks every black-and-white engraving listed in a book's ledger through one chosen colouring method, then hands the results and the ledger onward." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A ledger sheet labelled manifest.yaml sits at upper left. A file of grey engraving prints leaves it and travels right to a junction with five branching chutes. A lever marked --tool selects one chute. The ai chute is drawn largest, with four parallel lanes feeding an image-edit model. Prints emerge from the model softly coloured, with ochre stone, muted greens and pale blue sky. They carry on toward an output folder at lower right. One print drops out of its lane into a tray marked as a failure.

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one shows two copies of the same engraving. One has a blue sky. The other is flagged no_sky, and its top keeps the engraving's own tone. circle two shows a tall engraving fitted to the nearest matching aspect ratio, so the framing is kept. circle three shows returned files named by their true bytes: JPEG from Gemini, PNG from OpenAI. The studies show, in order, the sepia chute, the copy chute, the deoldify chute and the python-script chute.

Colour is used so that Warm ochre marks colour added by a tool. Pale blue marks sky. Red marks a failed image set aside. Neutral grey marks untouched originals.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 5 colouring tools at the junction. 4 parallel workers by default on the ai chute. 2 destinations, the output folder and the --copy-to folder. 9 aspect ratios considered when fitting the framing.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: manifest.yaml on the ledger sheet and its copy. --tool on the selector lever. ai, sepia, deoldify, python-script and copy on their chutes. --workers on the four lanes. no_sky on the flagged engraving. --copy-to on the second folder. JPEG and PNG on the returned files. Gemini and OpenAI on the model sources.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: manifest.yaml, engravings in, --tool, ai, sepia, deoldify, python-script, copy (default), image-edit model, --workers. no_sky, no blue sky, nearest aspect ratio, Gemini returns JPEG, OpenAI returns PNG. warm brown tone, originals unchanged, if installed, your own script. output folder, manifest copied, --copy-to, second folder. failed image skipped, rerun fills gaps, never fatal.

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Every listed engraving takes the chosen path; Workers send model calls side by side. Flagged images get a sky-free prompt; Output keeps the engraving's own framing. Copy lets the pipeline proceed while colour waits. Ledger travels on for downstream stages. Failure is reported, then the line continues.
